title: Haversine distance — Geospatial Search
description: Haversine computes great-circle distance between latitude/longitude points on a spherical Earth. The formula uses sines of half-differences, remaining numerically stable for nearby points. It is the default distance for 'near me' queries worldwide.

title: Bounding-box queries — Geospatial Search
description: A bounding box (min/max lat/lon) filters candidates with four cheap comparisons before any distance math. Boxes prune the vast majority of points; exact distance then ranks survivors. Every spatial index uses box filtering as its first pass.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: R-tree spatial index — Geospatial Search
description: R-trees group nearby points into nested minimum bounding rectangles. Queries descend only branches whose rectangles intersect the search area. R-trees make spatial filtering logarithmic instead of linear.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Geohash encoding — Geospatial Search
description: Geohash interleaves lat/lon bits into a base-32 string where shared prefixes mean nearby cells. Prefix length sets precision: longer strings, smaller cells. Geohashes turn 2-D proximity into 1-D prefix queries any database can serve.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: K-nearest neighbors — Geospatial Search
description: KNN queries return the k closest points regardless of distance, answering 'the 5 nearest'. Best-first traversal of the spatial index expands the most promising branches first. KNN needs no radius guess, which users appreciate.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Point-in-polygon tests — Geospatial Search
description: Ray casting counts boundary crossings: odd means inside, even means outside. It answers 'which district contains this address' for arbitrary polygons. Polygon tests power every geofencing system.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Route and corridor search — Geospatial Search
description: Corridor queries find points within distance d of a polyline route. Each route segment becomes a capsule; points test against nearby segments via the spatial index. Corridor search answers 'what is along my drive'.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Spatial joins — Geospatial Search
description: Spatial joins pair records from two datasets by geometric predicates like WITHIN or INTERSECTS. Plane-sweep and index-nested-loop algorithms keep joins tractable. Joins connect, say, sensor readings to the districts containing them.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Coordinate reference systems — Geospatial Search
description: Coordinates are meaningless without their CRS; WGS84 (GPS) differs from local projected systems by meters to kilometers. Transforms reproject between systems before comparison. Mixing CRS silently is the classic geospatial bug.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Reverse geocoding — Geospatial Search
description: Reverse geocoding turns coordinates into place names via point-in-polygon over administrative boundaries. Hierarchical lookup returns street, district, city, country in one pass. It is how apps label a raw GPS fix.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Temporal-spatial queries — Geospatial Search
description: Moving objects add time: queries ask 'where was it between 2 and 3pm' or 'which vehicles crossed this zone'. Trajectories index as space-time polylines with 3-D bounding boxes. Spatio-temporal indexes serve fleet and wildlife tracking.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Density heatmaps — Geospatial Search
description: Heatmaps aggregate point density into grid cells for visualization. Kernel density estimation smooths counts so hotspots emerge. They turn millions of points into one glanceable image.
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Geofencing alerts — Geospatial Search
description: Geofences trigger actions on polygon entry/exit, evaluated as streaming point-in-polygon tests. Indexing fences spatially keeps per-event checks cheap at fleet scale. Logistics and safety systems run on geofence events.

title: Map tile pyramids — Geospatial Search
description: Tile pyramids pre-render map zoom levels into 256px squares addressed by z/x/y. Clients fetch only visible tiles, caching aggressively. Pyramids are why web maps pan smoothly over planet-scale data.

title: Privacy in location search — Geospatial Search
description: Location queries leak movement; k-anonymity and geo-indistinguishability add calibrated noise. Systems return areas instead of points when precision is not needed. Privacy-preserving geo search is mandatory for personal data.
